subject: humanities
passage: Composed chess problems, positions constructed to be solved rather than played, are judged by standards that have little to do with competitive chess. A composer may reject a position because the winning move is too obvious, because a second, unintended solution exists, or simply because the pieces are arranged without economy. For composers, such flaws are not ______; an extra solution ruins a problem as surely as a false note ruins a melody, even though a player at the board would happily take either route to victory.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The semicolon introduces the reason: an extra solution "ruins" a problem, even though a player would not mind it. So for composers these flaws are serious, not minor; "trivial" is the word the sentence denies.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The second solution is described as "unintended"; whether flaws are deliberate is not the contrast the sentence draws.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says an extra solution ruins the problem, so for composers the flaw is fatal; the sentence needs a word for what the flaws are not.
explanation.C: Correct. The flaws "ruin" a problem for composers, so composers do not regard them as minor, even though a player would.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text does not discuss whether such flaws can be avoided, only how seriously composers take them.
